today.h: Stocks Fall a Second Day as Yields Camp at 19-Year Highs; Oil Gives Back Its War Spike
today.c1: A second straight down day, but a quieter one: the S&P slipped 0.17% while Treasury yields camped at their highest since 2007 and oil gave back part of its war spike (WTI -3.9%). Under the surface three stories diverged — memory and Meta bounced but couldn't lift the tape; FICO lost a quarter of its value on one policy post; and a consumer-confidence reading that hasn't been this glum since 2014 set the stagflation tension before Wednesday's PCE and Friday's payrolls.
today.c4:
• Holding pattern into PCE (Wed) and payrolls (Fri): keep duration short — every yield uptick is still sold (watch 5.30% on the 10Y).
  • Trade the oil relief, don't marry it: Saudi pipe flows vs. 'offered Iran nothing' — a real Hormuz deal is the reversal trigger.
  • Two-speed AI: capital keeps flowing ($2T Anthropic IPO, AMD's $8.2B World Labs); buy the picks-and-shovels dips, question the story stocks.

chains.t: ① Main Chain: The Yield Grind Extends — a Second Down Day Into 19-Year Highs
steps: Dow worst of majors (-0.5% midday); breadth 2:1 negative
chains.d: Roughly 60% of today's grind: with the Fed priced to hike again, every rally into fresh yield highs got sold — and the oil retreat was the one valve holding the tape up.

news.fact: The 10Y closed near 5.26% (+2bp) after printing above 5.29% intraday — highest since 2007 — capping a ~30bp rise over six sessions; the 30Y at 5.59% is back to 2002 levels.
Midday washout: Dow -0.54%, S&P -0.21%, Nasdaq -0.06%; nine of 11 sectors lower, chips rebounding (+1.8% PHLX) and NYSE decliners ahead of advancers 2.18-to-1.
NY Fed's Williams: 'no need for urgency' on another hike; one more move may be appropriate 'late this year' — pushback on October pricing, which sits at ~68-73%.
The other lens on the same pressure: the Shiller CAPE is at its highest since 1999 — valuations remain the market's open flank.

chains.t: ② Oil Cracks: Supply Comes Back, the War Premium Deflates
steps: Mediation talk — but Trump: 'offered Iran nothing'
Still ~1/3 above pre-war ($67) — a valve, not an exit
chains.d: The day's biggest asset move. Cheaper crude cools the inflation tail that's been feeding the yield surge — which is why stocks didn't extend Monday's rout. A real Hormuz deal is the reversal trigger.

news.fact: WTI settled near $89 — down 3.6-3.9% depending on the quote — and Brent fell 2.6% to ~$102.55 as Saudi Arabia ramped exports through its East-West pipeline; WTI remains far above the ~$67 pre-war level.
Trump said he 'offered Iran nothing' to end the war, rejecting reports he was willing to extend sanctions relief; still no sign of progress toward a peace deal.
As regional exports rebound and Iran's grip on Hormuz loosens, the mirror risk rises: Tehran could escalate militarily to reassert leverage.

chains.t: ③ Landmine of the Day: FICO's Moat Cracks (-27%)
steps: Pulte post: one GSE pricing grid
Rocket Mortgage flips to VantageScore in Q4
chains.d: Half of FICO's year is gone because a regulator posted on X — the day's cautionary tale on policy-made moats. Apple's slide was the quieter index drag beneath the surface.

news.fact: FICO plunged ~27% after FHFA Director Bill Pulte moved Fannie and Freddie to one pricing grid with VantageScore as an equal; Rocket Mortgage became the first major lender to adopt VantageScore 4.0 as its default model for eligible loans.
Reuters measured FICO -26.4% by late morning; Monday's pre-crash close had already left the stock down ~50% for the year.
Winners: Carnival +14% (best in the S&P, on record revenue and a raised outlook) and CarMax +5% after earnings — travel and used cars led the gainers.
Apple -2.7% led mega-cap declines (MAGS -0.2%); Tesla -1.3% after pushing its Roadster reveal to Oct 15.

chains.t: ④ AI Two-Speed Tape: Capital Keeps Flowing; Valuations Keep Grinding
steps: NVDA fades to -0.7%; OpenAI holds back 'Astra'
chains.d: The bull case (money never stops: $2T IPOs, $8B deals) and the bear case (losses, delays, high prices) traded side by side all day — dips get bought in capex names; story stocks get sold into every yield tick.

news.fact: Anthropic's IPO papers (via Reuters): ~$4.6B revenue last year vs $400M the year prior, $8B+ operating losses, and a targeted $2T-plus valuation — potentially a record IPO, expected in November.
AMD agreed to buy Fei-Fei Li's physical-AI startup World Labs for $8.2B in stock (announced Monday); Li joins as EVP & chief scientist. AMD shares: -3.6% Monday, flat Tuesday.
Memory and chips rebounded after Monday's rout — DRAM ETF +3%, SOXX +1%, PHLX semis +1.8%; Meta +3.2% on Muse tools for small business; Nvidia closed down less than 1%.
OpenAI is holding back its next model ('GPT-6.1 Astra') over alignment and scope concerns — execution risk sits alongside the hype (WSJ).

chains.t: ⑤ The Consumer Cracks: Confidence at 2014 Lows Into the Data Double-Header
steps: Soft data — yet yields rose anyway (stagflation math)
Swings ahead: PCE Wednesday, payrolls Friday
chains.d: Bad news stopped being good news: weak demand data couldn't pull yields down while oil-driven inflation still rules. Wednesday's PCE (expected 3.7%) and Friday's jobs report decide whether that flips.

news.fact: Consumer confidence fell 6.7 points to 81.9 in September — the lowest since 2014 and far below the 89 consensus; for the first time in the question's four-year history, more respondents said their finances were 'bad' than 'good'.
JOLTS: openings fell 256k to 7.079M in August (forecast: ~7.2M) — fewest since March; hires rose slightly and layoffs hit their lowest since March 2025, a low-hire, low-fire market.
TSA checkpoint counts are running ~5% below their 2024 peak — a 'canary in the coal mine' for consumer spending, per Pantheon Macroeconomics.
Next up: August PCE on Wednesday (expected +3.7% y/y) plus Micron earnings; the September jobs report lands Friday.

mtd.h: September's Round-Trip: A Hawkish Fed Wipes Out the Month; the Dow's Worst September in Three Years
mtd.d: S&P -0.20% on the month; the Dow's -3.4% is its worst September in three years — with one session left.
mtd.c1: 8/31 7686 → 9/29 7671: the month round-tripped from positive to slightly negative. The 9/16 hike plus a hawkish Warsh was the watershed; the 9/21 AI record has been fully given back. Underneath, tech held (+4%) while everything else bled — materials, financials and consumer names are down 6%+.
mtd.c4:
• 60/40 stopped working again this month; energy and tech were the only real shelters.
  • September ends Wednesday — October hinges on PCE and payrolls for a back-to-back hike.

chains.t: ① The Fed Turns Hawkish — the MTD Core
chains.d: Powell → Warsh: from pricing cuts to pricing hikes — that flip is September's story.

news.fact: Fed hiked +25bp to 3.75-4.00%; Warsh warned on inflation; Dow -600pts on the day.
Oil pulled back and jobs held; Nasdaq led a rebound as the market digested the hike.
10Y +13.9bp to 5.106% (highest since 2007, biggest one-day jump since April 2025); Nasdaq's record streak ended.
Six sessions later the 10Y sits at 5.26% — up ~50bp on the month — and the 30Y has climbed to 5.59%.

chains.d: September reversed weekly; every deal-hope rally was a sale — until supply normalization finally flipped the drift this week.

news.fact: 10Y back above 4.8%; oil rose into the CPI wait; on 9/9 WTI topped $100.
Last week rallied on Hormuz-reopening hopes; after the weekend rejection, 9/28 gave it all back.
Tuesday's move went the other way — WTI -3.6~3.9% on Saudi pipeline flows, its biggest drop in weeks.

chains.t: ③ AI Splits at the Highs
chains.d: The index is flat on the month; the rotation underneath is violent.

news.fact: S&P 7764.7 +1.49%; Nasdaq 27122 +2.26%, a record; AMD reached a $1T market cap.
Utilities fell to a more-than-one-year low as the AI power-demand narrative backfired.

chains.d: A weak Dow means institutions cutting blue chips into Wednesday's close; flows amplify the drift.

news.fact: S&P 7686.14 -0.3%, Dow 53185.9 -0.7% — the MTD starting line.
September ends Wednesday: S&P -0.2% MTD, Dow -3.4% — its worst September in three years.

qtd.h: Q3 Nears the Finish at +2.29%: July's Earnings Run Gives Way to September's Yield Shock
qtd.d: 6/30 7499 → 9/29 7671, +2.29%; the quarter peaked at 7799 in August and spent September giving gains back.
qtd.c1: July rode earnings to new highs, August stalled at the 7800 line, and September gave part of it back — the quarter ends Wednesday with the S&P up 2.3% and the Dow down 1.9%. The spoiler is the same everywhere: the 10Y +84bp to 5.26%.
qtd.c4:
• Protect the +2.3%: quarter-end games end Wednesday — don't chase into the print.
  • Energy (+16% QTD) and health (+8%) carried; utilities (-12%) were the rate trade's casualty.

chains.d: The numerator can't outrun the denominator: a 2.3% net gain after a 4% peak.

news.fact: S&P 7499.36 +0.79%, Dow 52319 (record), Nasdaq 26213; Q2 was the best in six years: S&P +15.2%, Nasdaq +21.4%.
WSJ: the best quarter in six years will be a hard act to follow.

chains.d: A global resonance, not just the U.S.

news.fact: Japan's Finance Minister Katayama: long-end yields are high because global AI-infrastructure capex needs funding.
JPM's Michele: the whole curve is oversold; the bond market may stabilize.

chains.d: Oil above $90 for the quarter is the regime, not a shock.

news.fact: U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran started the conflict; Iran retaliated and the strait was weaponized.
Saudi supply restoration knocks prices down, blockade pushes them up — still the only swing factor.

chains.d: The index lies; money crowds into themes.

news.fact: As of Monday: the quarter's gains were mostly mega-caps; memory, software and power-demand names lagged.

ytd.h: The Bull Market Holds Into Q4: +12% for the S&P as +110bp of Rates Rewrite the Playbook
ytd.d: S&P +12.06%, Nasdaq +15.30% — gains from AI and earnings; headaches from rates and war.
ytd.c1: The rally extended 2025's +16%, breaking 50k in February and 52k in June. The 10Y's move from 4.16% to 5.26% is the year's biggest variable — and gold, after spiking with the war, is now down ~3% on the year.
ytd.c4:
• With a +12% cushion, don't chase; keep duration short.
  • Rebalance into energy; re-add gold only if real yields peak.

chains.d: The base case isn't broken; April's plunge V-shaped back in Q2.

news.fact: S&P 6845.5 -0.74%, Dow 48063 -0.63%, Nasdaq 23241 -0.76% on the final day — but 2025 still posted a third straight up year: S&P +16%, Nasdaq +19%, Dow +13%.
Dow H1 +8.9%, its best first half since 2021; S&P Q2 +15.2%, best since 2020.
PCE has run above target for five years and Warsh is watching inflation; August PCE lands Wednesday (expected +3.7%).

chains.d: The rally and rising rates share one root: AI needs money.

news.fact: NVDA +25% YTD with a $235B buyback; the capex cycle keeps compounding.
2026's capital cycle: AMD's $8.2B World Labs deal and a targeted $2T-plus Anthropic listing headline a year of relentless AI investment.

chains.d: Every deal-hope rally was a sale.

news.fact: The 7-day plan rejection is the latest falsification this year; mediators (Qatar) keep working.
The dollar is +0.2% today at 101.38 (+~3% YTD); gold's war spike has fully retraced — it's down ~3% on the year.
